semantic.label: Evening transfer for the coastal laboratory
Match the seal number to the coastal manifest before moving the crate. Keep a damaged seal in the current freezer and call the receiving technician.
Clear the coastal receiving shelf and put its tray within reach. Leave other specimens in their labeled compartments while the new crate is being placed.
Carry the crate with its insulated lid latched. Open it inside the receiving cold room after the technician checks the destination and prepares the logger.
Use the marked indoor corridor. Ask a colleague to hold the internal door so the crate does not wait beside an exterior entrance.
Read the logger with its probe still in the packing sleeve. Record the displayed temperature and arrival time on the manifest before replacing the lid.
Put a container with a loose cap or damaged label in the secondary tray. Ask the technician to verify its identity before writing a replacement label.
Wait for the technician to acknowledge the crate identifier. This app records the release request; the receiving team completes its separate physical inventory and signature.
Place the signed manifest in the cold-room sleeve. Keep the crate identifier facing the aisle so the next shift can find the specimens and their record.
